content.title: French Quarter Festival 2026 WWL Coverage
content.text: Watch French Quarter Fest live with music, food and exclusive interviews from Thursday, April 16 through Sunday, April 19 on WWL. NEW ORLEANS — WWL Louisiana is livestreaming French Quarter Fest starting Thursday, bringing you live coverage straight from the heart of New Orleans! Expect interviews with musicians, local chefs, and vendors, plus a closer look at the food and culture that make the festival special. Thursday, April 16 Starting at 10 a.m., WWL will stream live coverage of the parade as it winds through the French Quarter toward Jackson Square for the opening ceremonies. Festival streaming coverage continues from 12:30 to 3:45 p.m., featuring Whitney Miller along with appearances by artists and food vendors. Guests include DJ Raj Smoove, a longtime New Orleans DJ known for blending hip-hop, R&B, and bounce, and Emily Madero, CEO of French Quarter Festivals Inc. DJ Raj Smoove is also performing Thursday from 7 to 8 p.m. on the Louisiana Fish Fry Stage. Ha Sizzle, the self-proclaimed King of Bounce, will join us for an interview before his set Sunday with the TBC Brass Band from 5 p.m. to 6:20 p.m. Dawn Richard, a New Orleans native and internationally known artist, will also sit down with us ahead of her Saturday performance on the Abita Beer Stage from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. See one of the most popular vendors at FQF, Loretta's Pralines, with Robert Harrison. They will talk about what makes the classic Creole sweet stand out, while chef Lauren Johnson-Blake of 14 Parishes will share dishes inspired by Caribbean flavors. Friday, April 17 Get ready for Whitney Miller and Great Day Louisiana host Malik Mingo as they take over Friday’s coverage from 12:30-4. Guests include Pell and Alfred Banks, New Orleans hip-hop artists known for strong lyrics and a sound that reflects the city, who’ll stop by ahead of their Friday set at the Loyola Esplanade's Shade Stage from 3:10 to 4:10 p.m. Also featured are Arsène Delay and Charlie Wooton, known for blending blues, funk, and soul, who’ll check in with us before their performance on the Pan-American Life Insurance Group Stage from 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. Ryan Batiste, part of the Batiste musical family, carries on a New Orleans legacy by blending tradition with a modern sound in his band, Ryan Batiste & the Raw Revolution. He’ll talk with us ahead of his Saturday performance on the Abita Beer Stage from 12:50 to 1:50 p.m. Lavelle Dunn will join us on the stream to talk about the culinary stage. They’ll be hosting there at the festival, bringing energy and personality to connect chefs with the audience and showcase festival food. Saturday, April 18 Coverage continues with Brheanna Boudreaux and Leigha McNeil from noon to 3:30 p.m., followed by the WWL sports team, Doug Mouton and Seth Lewis, through 7 p.m. Guests include Daphne Parker Powell, a singer-songwriter known for blending jazz, folk, and pop influences. DJ Hollaback will talk about his high-energy sets that keep the crowds moving. He’ll also perform on Saturday on the Louisiana Fish Fry Stage from 12:35 to 1:05 p.m. Grammy-winning zydeco artist Corey Ledet will highlight the genre’s deep Louisiana roots. He performs on the Willow Dispensary Stage from 3:30 to 4:40 p.m. Marlon Williams of Chicken’s Kitchen will also showcase classic New Orleans comfort food. Sunday, April 19 The final day features Chief Meteorologist Chris Franklin, Lily Cummings, and Malik Mingo. Casme performs on Sunday, the final day of the festival, at the Loyola Esplanade on the Shade Stage from 11 a.m. to noon, and will join us after their performance. Mayumi Shara also performs on Sunday at the French Market Dutch Alley Stage from 12:45 to 2 p.m., and will join us following their show. Vance Vaucresson, a fourth-generation Creole food producer, will discuss preserving traditional flavors. Our coverage will wrap up with Harry Mayronne and Chloe Marie, known for their piano-driven sound with a modern New Orleans touch. Parking and traffic restrictions for French Quarter Festival 2026 Street closures A 10 a.m. parade will trigger rolling street closures as it moves through the French Quarter en route to Jackson Square for opening ceremonies. The following streets along the route will be closed: Bourbon Street from the 200 block (Iberville Street) to St. Ann StreetSt. Ann Street from Bourbon Street to Chartres StreetChartres Street from St. Ann Street to Jackson Square At noon, police will expand closures, restricting access beyond checkpoints to residents, businesses and hotel guests. These restrictions remain in effect daily through Sunday evening: Bourbon Street from Canal Street to Dumaine Street (crossing may be allowed at St. Peter Street)Royal Street from Conti Street to St. Peter StreetDecatur Street from Conti Street to St. Peter StreetNorth Peters Street from Conti Street to St. Louis StreetGeneral boundaries: Exterior and interior closures span from Canal Street to Dumaine Street and from Decatur Street to North Rampart Street. No-parking zones The city will ban parking on both sides of major streets throughout the Quarter from noon Thursday through 1 a.m. Monday, April 20. Any vehicle in these zones will be ticketed and towed: A–C: Barracks Street, Bienville Street, Canal Street, Chartres Street, Conti StreetD–I: Dauphine Street, Decatur Street, Elysian Fields Avenue, Esplanade Avenue, Iberville StreetM–R: Madison Street, North Front Street, North Peters Street, Orleans Avenue, Royal StreetS–W: St. Ann Street, St. Louis Street, St. Peter Street, St. Philip Street, Toulouse Street, Wilkinson Row Superintendent Anne Kirkpatrick confirmed enforcement will be heavily resourced. "We’re going to have extra tow trucks out there, and it’s for a reason," Kirkpatrick said. "I take no pleasure in taking your car, but I will. Please do your part." Transportation alternatives Officials are encouraging people to walk, bike or take public transportation to get around. Ferry service: Service between Algiers Point and Canal Street will include a second vessel to reduce wait times. On Thursday and Sunday, last departures are 8:30 p.m. from Algiers and 8:45 p.m. from Canal Street. On Friday and Saturday, extended departures will run at 10:30 p.m. from Algiers and 10:45 p.m. from Canal Street. Ferry queuing on the West Bank will be rerouted along the levee due to construction.Regional Transit Authority: Buses and streetcars will run along key routes serving the festival area, including the Canal Street and Riverfront/UPT lines. While delays are likely, the RTA will adjust service as needed. Riders can use the Le Pass app for live updates.Rideshare: Drop-offs and pickups are encouraged along Canal Street and Esplanade Avenue, where congestion is more manageable.Golf carts: Attendees are reminded that golf carts are strictly prohibited within festival areas. For assistance with parking enforcement or to locate a towed vehicle, call 504-658-8100.
